title: Decomposing a House Drawing
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Computational Thinking
Decomposition
Turtle Graphics
Scratch
description: Clickable tree diagram that decomposes the job 'draw a house' across four levels, from the whole job down to single Scratch blocks. Clicking a box tells the student whether that piece is small enough to program, gives the reason, and highlights the path back to the top job.

learningObjectives: Given a drawing task, identify which parts of the task are still too big to program and which parts are small enough to become a single instruction.
prerequisites: A program is a list of steps done in order

controls.label: Tree boxes
controls.description: Click a box to see whether it is small enough to program and to highlight its path to the top job; hover for a Yes / Not yet tooltip

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then click to check; path highlighting links each small step to the big job it belongs to
keyQuestions: Which boxes are small enough to be one Scratch block?
Why is 'Draw one side' not small enough yet?
Which big job does 'Turn right 120 degrees' belong to?
commonMisconceptions: A step that sounds short, such as 'turn one corner', is already precise. It is not, because it does not say how far to turn.
Every corner is a 90 degree turn. A triangle corner is a 120 degree turn.
assessmentOpportunities: Ask the student to predict Yes or Not yet for each box before clicking.
Have the student draw a decomposition tree for a new drawing job.
